dedupe_keys.name: systemicrisk matlab framework covar mes srisk and network measures

description: SystemicRisk is a MATLAB framework that computes a wide range of systemic risk measures from market and balance sheet data: cross-sectional measures such as CoVaR, marginal expected shortfall (MES), SRISK and CAViaR; network measures such as the dynamic causality index and betweenness, degree, closeness and eigenvector centrality; default measures such as distance to default, distance to capital and the distress insurance premium; liquidity, tail dependence and spillover indices; and regime-switching and bubble detection models. It is written and published by Tommaso Belluzzo and was featured in the MATLAB Digest for financial services in May 2019. It applies to any set of listed financial firms; the input is an Excel workbook of daily observations with at least 253 prices or 252 returns for at least three firms. The code is free under the Apache 2.0 licence, but MATLAB R2014b or later is needed. Caveats: it is a single-author project whose examples use data to 2019, so it is marked stale, and market-based measures reflect investor perceptions, not exposures. For simulation it quantifies how distress in one institution spills over to others, giving network and tail-risk inputs to cascading failure and resilience studies of the financial sector. It is related to the resilience library record in this catalogue, which simulates contagion mechanisms directly.
